headline: Approved plans for subdivisions at 190 Hampstead Road and 34 Pingree Hill Road, plus a driveway culvert at 1 Family Ridge Drive.
summary: Commissioners approved three projects with conditions, including straw bales for erosion control and invasive species language on the plans. They also approved a $40 payment to N.H.A.C.C. for two handbooks. The minutes also cover land management, outreach, and subcommittee updates.
decisions: Approved the minutes of September 28, 2026, unanimously.
Approved signing the subdivision plans for 190 Hampstead Road with four stipulations, unanimously.
Approved the subdivision plan for 34 Pingree Hill Road with two stipulations and authorized the Chair to sign, unanimously.
Approved the driveway culvert plan for 1 Family Ridge Drive with stipulations and permission for the Chair to sign the expedited application to D.E.S., unanimously.
Approved a $40 check to N.H.A.C.C. for two handbooks from the Administrative Account, unanimously.

Driveway culvert at 1 Family Ridge Drive

plain_text:
Derry Conservation Commission
Municipal Center
Derry, NH
October 5, 2026
-Callto Order: Chairman Buzzanga calledthe meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., he led the Pledge of Allegiance.
-RollCall: Riccardo Buzzanga, Rick Metts, Robert Spoerl,Eileen Chabot, Linda Comrie, Chery! Holbert,Jay
Hildreth,Land Manager Beth Carver, and Council LiaisonCharlie Foote.
-Approval of Minutes:
 
Commission Metts MOVED to approve the Minutes of September 28, 2026, that includesthe correctionof
the date. Commissioner Chabot seconded the Motion.
Vote: Unanimous   
-Correspondence: The Commission met a week prior, and no correspondence has been received since.
-Chair’sReport: Chairman Buzzanga updated that there was communication about one of the parcelsthe
Commission is tryingto preserve with the landowner. Southeast Land Trust of NH (S.E.L.T.)provided resources
in selectingan appraiser with bids and one that was chosen who the Commission isfamiliarwith. The
landowner has agreed.
-ResidentialSubdivision:Map 10 Lot 7-1:Address 190 Hampstead Road; Owner Name and Address: Richard J.
Ward, 190 Hampstead Road, Derry NH 03038. Surveyor: Keach-Nordstrom Associates,Inc.5 Commerce Park
North, Suite 201, Bedford NH 03110. Presenter: Peter Madsen, PE.
-Mr. Madsen camebefore the Commission representingthe applicant,TJB Holmes, LLC. to present this2-lot
sub-division.This lothas a parent parcel consistingof 5 acres that iscurrentlydeveloped with an existing2-
storysinglefamily home with a driveway from Hampstead Road. They would liketo sub-dividethe property to
create one newlot for a single-familyhome. The newlot will consistof justunder 2 % acres leavingthe
remaininglot with a littleover 2 % acres.The existinghouse isserviced by an onsitewell and septic.The new
house isproposed for the same. Itisnoted on the plans on the west side of the property an isolatedwetland
pocket that isassociated with someof the drainage along Hampstead Road. The planis a proposal for a 4-
bedroom single-familyhome with a 130-foot driveway offof Hampstead Road. They willnot be disturbingany
wetlands or anything within the 30-foot buffer.The leach fielddesign andfinal septicare stillpending. Mr.
Madsen states thefull design plans willmeet allapplicablesetbacks. Chairman Buzzanga spoke about the
protected well radiusand referredto the 75-foot setback. He reiteratedthat the wetland bufferwould not be
disturbed.Chairman Buzzanga asked Mr. Madsen to add to the plans the Commissions’ invasiveparagraph that
speaks about using the best practiceswhen dealing with invasivespecies.Also,the plan willshow straw
instead of hay whenit comesto erosion control measures. Commissioner Chabot asked that the straw bales
not be moved untilthe sitehas fullystabilizedwith vegetation.Lastly,the plan willadhere to setback
requirements from the wetland on the leachfield and septicsystem.
 
Commissioner Metts MOVED to have the Chair sign the plans with the 4 stipulations.Commissioner Hildreth
seconded the Motion.
Vote: Unanimous
-3-LotSubdivision Plan:Map 14 Lot 24: Address: 34 Pingree HillRd; Owner: Craig J.Bonneau Construction,22
Gulf Road; Surveyor: Edward N. Herbert Assoc. Inc,Paul Zarnowski LLS.1 FrostRoad, Windham, NH 03867;
Presenter: Shayne Gendron, P.E.
-Mr. Gendron beganhis presentation speaking about the 8-acre parcelthat willbe subdivided intothreelots.
Oneof thelots willbe improved with a single-familyhome with a driveway, septicsystem and well.This plan
has been presented before the Technical Review Committee and has received comments. They have walked
the property with the Derry PublicWorks Department which they then requested some improvements. Those
plans have been updated although he currentlydoes not have theinvasive species paragraph added to plans
justyet.There isabout 1400 feet of road frontage on thislotand 440 feet of road frontage on Winchester
Terrace.The Zoning Board provided relieffor map and lot14-21-1 as itdoes not meet the three-acre
requirement. The center 3-acre lotwillstaywith the existinghome. Map 14 Lot 24 -1 has a variancefor a 2.3-
acre lotdoes have a wetland buffer.The plans show the 75-foot buffer,and everything isstayingaway from it.
They willbe providingsilt fence (statedin the plans),and they are also providing driplineinfiltrationaroundall
the homes. Leachfields are both more than 120 feet away from the wetlands. Two detailson the plan include
a four-footshoulder and the other isfor a four-footgravel shoulder with a shallow swale, 6 inches and grated
four to one. Chairman Buzzanga askedif there were any culvertshe was missing. Mr. Gendron answered there
wasan existing culvertunder Pingree Hillso the wetland sortof divides lot14 24-1 and lot24 and Derry Public
Works has asked them to clean upthe inleton theirside.Itisan existing12-inch RCP. There was discussionon
whatthe State requiresfor testpits.Chairman Buzzanga asked ifon the two new lotswere outside the
protectivewet well radiusand outside the wetland setback area. Mr. Gendronreplied that itwas true.
Chairman Buzzangaasked if the siltfence detailscould be added to the plans along with straw bales instead of
hay and the bales to remain untilthe vegetation grows back. The invasivespecies language should be added
to the plans and the erosion controls/linetype added to the legend.
 
Commissioner Metts MOVED to approvethe plan with the twostipulations and for the Chair to sign the
plan.Commissioner Comrie seconded the Motion.
Vote: Unanimous   
-Driveway Culvert; Map 9, Lot 1; Address: 1 Family Ridge Drive (offShurman Drive); Owner Name and
Address: Grant Benson P.O.Box 444 Derry, NH 03038; Surveyor Name and Address: Kevin E. Hatch LLS,
Cornerstone Survey, Associate,25 Whitetail Lane, Chester NH 03036; Presenter:Kevin Hatch, PE.
-Mr. Hatch reviewed for the Commission the land had originallybeen introduced as a 14-lotsubdivision,but
the owner would now liketo scale thisback to a two-lot subdivision.There isan existinghouse on the
property,and they would liketo subdivide to create another 9-acre lot.Mr. Hatch further explained they would
need a driveway culvertas there isa short crossingon that 9-acre lot.The plan isfor a common driveway offof
Sherman Drive going to the 13-acre parcel.The 13-acre willbe subdivided with thisnew lotbeing nine acres
with a driveway culvert.That culvertwillhave about 600-foot impact. The wetlands have beenflagged with
the crossing being minimized as muchas possible. The old crossingfor the 14-lotsubdivisionbecause of allthe
road design standards, was about 1900 square feet.The driveway willbe moved at the narrowercrossing
locationand moved downto 600 square feet.The proposalwill put the house on the 9-acre lot.They are
currentlyapplying for the expediated drudge andfill as itmeets the expedited requirements with this
Commissions’ approval. They willlaterapply for sub-divisionapproval and are asking for the Commissions
signature on the subdivisionplan.Chairman Buzzangaclarified thiswas for culvertplacement whichwill later
be approved by the Department of Environmental Services and then they would returnto the Commission. Mr.
Hatch explained the focusof the subdivisionwas the culvert.Mr. Hatch shared a copyof the expediated permit
2
with the Commission. Discussionensued regarding process and protocols.Commissioner Chabot askedif there
was a stream on the plans that were being shown. Mr. Hatchclarified itwas not a stream. She asked about the
minimum impactlisted on the expedited permit. Chairman Buzzangaclarified for thisevening Mr. Hatch would
need a communication from the Commission Chair to the applicantsaying the Conservation Commission has
reviewed the wetland impact and has no objectionto it.Chairman Buzzanga summarized the Commissions’
evasive language, straw bales and leavingthem untilthe vegetation grows back would be neededto add to the
plans.
 
Commissioner Metts MOVED to approvethe culvertplan with the stipulationsmentioned beforehand and
give the Chair permission to sign the expedited applicationto D.E.S.Commissioner Holbert seconded the
Motion.
Vote: Unanimous   
-Chairman Buzzanga spoke of the agenda and how they have moved the Land Managers report earlierinthe
meeting in order for the Commissioners and publicto receive a fullreport of current events happening and the
continuous work Beth Carver does.
Land Manager Report: Ms. Carver began her reportwith an update with the Community WildfireProtection
Plan (CSPP) which has been added to the Town Council Agenda on October 20, 2026. Cub Scout Troop 402 met
at Broadview Farm along with a few members of the Greater Derry Track Club. They did sometrail
maintenance work around the wooded trails leading to the camping area. The scouts spread out some brush
and the adults worked with hand tools to widenthe trail. Derry PublicWorks cleared some overgrowth at
Broadview and invasivespecies from the area near the gardens which willbe the new locationsfor clean
cemetery leaves.They also installeda small access drive.Derry PublicWorks were also able to salvage the
largewooden two bay compost bin. Regarding the Ball,Corneliusen and Fernando propertiesand the Rapid
Response Committee, Ms. Carver has spoken with Vicky Smith. She oversees the Produce Safety Program with
the Department of Agriculture.She said that farms need to have a policyin how they willaddress domestic
animals on theirfarmland. Signage can be used to help prevent the publicfrom allowing domestic animals to
roam, whichis part of the conditions the Rapid Response Committee has set.Ms. Smithis willingto jointhe
conversations in the future.Chairman Buzzanga stated that many people use the Conservation lands and lands
were bought with town dollarsand he referredto equity.Chairman Buzzanga stated whenan established long-
term policyiscreated, itisbased on realfacts.Ms. Carver referredto Ms. Smiths’ involvementas sheis
knowledgeable. In her opinion,she feltthe farmers should be able to disallow dogs in croplands.Conversation
ensued.
The Commission received correspondence from the Democratic Socialistsof America. Their group would liketo
volunteer to help with a trailwork event. Cole Marsh was suggested. The group hasasked if they could use the
Commissions website and logo for advertisingthe event. Commissioner Comrie thought that the group would
be indicatingthat they are working along with the Commission as a partnerto dotrail cleanup. Chairman
Buzzanga asked that the advertisement be sent to the Commission priorto the event for the Commissions’
approval.
-Community Gardens: Commissioner Hildrethupdated the gardeners at Broadview were continuing to harvest
theirgardens such as butternut squash, tomatoes andresilient Swiss chard. He spoke of potentialfrostin the
area. A future subcommittee meeting willbe held for the November clean up eventthat isbeing planned.
-Broadview Annex: Commissioner Hildrethreferredto the discussionto be held on October 7, 2026, the Annex
Subcommittee would liketo meet with Beth Carver and ClintHavens to discusshow to manage trail creation
and mowing.
-Personnel: Commissioner Metts reported no new updates.
-TRC:Commissioner Metts updated therewillbe a reviewcoming up ina few weeks.
-Public Outreach: Commissioner Holbert thanked her fellow commissioners for theirwork ontrail heads and
socialmedia posts.The summer was active with the Farmers Market and Derry Fest.
-EnvironmentalPolicy & Training:Commissioner Chabot provided reminders for the N.H.A.C. Annual Meeting
being held on November 7, 2026. The Conservation Easement presentation by S.E.L.T.willbe held at the East
Kingston Libraryon October 21, 2026.
-Property Management: Chairman Buzzanga stated that he and Land Manager, Beth Carver continue to work
on ongoing projects,they are completed as they happen. Any projectsthat require any expenditure on funds
are reviewed during meetings.
-Land Acquisition:Chairman Buzzanga updated an agreement with an appraisalcompany has been reached to
appraise a property the Commission isconsidering conserving.They continue to pursue two other properties
as well.
-Rapid Response Subcommittee: The subcommittee continues to workin the fact-findingphase as Ms. Carver
continuesto get the detailsfrom the stakeholders.A second meeting willdecide what the long-term strategies
willbe. Ms. Carveris also researching what other communities are doing asthis isa state-wide problem.
 
-Land Maintenance: Commissioner Spoer| stated there were no updates.
-Reporting Compliance: Commissioner Comrie has offeredto chair thissubcommittee.
-Net Zero Task Force: Land Manger, Beth Carver hasoffered to attend meetings and then a decisionwill be
madeas to how muchviable work the Task Force has with the Commission and itsmission.Commissioner
Chabot spoke about budgeting matters.
-Council Liaison Report: Councilman Foote spoke of the retirement of Sheila Bodenrader whowill be missed
and wished herwell in her retirement.
OtherBusiness: Future meetings include the dates December 14, 2026, January 4, 2026, and January 18, 2026.
Discussiontook place regarding upcoming sitewalks and the scheduling of them.
 
Commissioner Metts MOVED to approve a $40 checkto go to N.H.A.C.C.for two handbooks to be taken out
of the AdministrativeAccount. Commissioner Holbert seconded the Motion.
Vote: Unanimous 
 
At 8:30 p.m., Commissioner Metts MOVED to adjourn. Commissioner Chabot seconded the Motion.
Vote: Unanimous   
RespectfullySubmitted,
Tammie Lampes
